instructions:
This server provides access to Arista EOS switches over eAPI and gNMI.
When EOS_READ_ONLY=true (default), it cannot change configuration; state-changing commands are rejected.

Choosing a target device:
- Most tools take a "device" argument. Prefer an IP address (e.g. "192.0.2.10").
  A configured device name or hostname also works. It is optional only when a
  single device is configured; fleet_* tools target many devices and list_devices takes no device.
- Some tools instead use "devices" (fleet_*), "device_a"/"device_b" (compare_*),
   or no device argument at all (list_devices).

Choosing a tool:
- "get_show_data" covers the curated read-only datasets: pass a "topic" from its
  enum (e.g. "bgp_summary", "interfaces_status", "mac_address_table"). Prefer it,
  or another specific tool, over "run_show_command".
- Use "run_show_command" only for read-only commands no topic or tool covers.
- For ONE command across MANY devices, use "fleet_run_command" / "fleet_get_version".
- To diff TWO devices, use "compare_config" or "compare_command".
- For an overall status check of one device, use "get_device_health".
- For reachability tests use "ping_host" / "traceroute_host".
- For model-driven telemetry or to watch values over time, use the gNMI tools
  ("gnmi_get" for a snapshot, "gnmi_subscribe" for a time window).

The "troubleshoot_*", "device_health_review", and "compare_devices" prompts
provide ready-made investigation workflows.

tools.description: Run the SAME command on TWO devices and diff the output lines. Use to compare specific state between a pair (e.g. 'show vlan', 'show ip bgp summary'). For full config use compare_config; for many devices use fleet_run_command.

command.description: the read-only command to run on both devices, e.g. 'show vlan'

tools.name: compare_command

tools.description: Diff the running-config of TWO devices and report lines unique to each. Use for 'what's different between A and B', config drift, consistency checks across a pair.
tools.name: compare_config

tools.description: Collect version/model/uptime from MANY devices (or all) in parallel. Use for fleet-wide inventory: 'what EOS version is everything running', model audit.

devices.description: target devices (IP preferred); empty means all configured devices

tools.name: fleet_get_version

tools.description: Run the SAME command on MANY devices (or all) in parallel and return a combined per-device report. Use for 'on all switches', 'across the fleet', bulk/sweep queries. For just two devices and a diff, use compare_command.

command.description: the read-only command to run on each device, e.g. 'show version'

devices.description: target devices (IP preferred); empty means all configured devices

tools.name: fleet_run_command

tools.description: Prefixes this device ADVERTISES to a specific BGP neighbor. Use for 'what are we sending to peer X', outbound policy checks. Runs 'show ip bgp neighbors <ip> advertised-routes'.

device.description: target device (IP preferred; name/hostname OK); optional if only one device is configured

tools.name: get_bgp_advertised_routes

tools.description: Prefixes RECEIVED from a specific BGP neighbor. Use for 'what is peer X sending us', inbound route/policy checks. Runs 'show ip bgp neighbors <ip> received-routes'.

device.description: target device (IP preferred; name/hostname OK); optional if only one device is configured

tools.name: get_bgp_received_routes

tools.description: One-shot overall health check of a SINGLE device: aggregates version, environment, interface status, port-channels, MLAG, and BGP into one report. Use for open-ended 'is this device healthy / what's its status' questions before drilling into a specific area.

device.description: target device (IP preferred; name/hostname OK); optional if only one device is configured

tools.name: get_device_health

tools.description: Full per-interface detail (state, counters, addresses, MTU, description). Use for a deep look at one or all interfaces; optionally filter by interface name. For a quick up/down overview prefer get_show_data topic 'interfaces_status'.

device.description: target device (IP preferred; name/hostname OK); optional if only one device is configured

interface.description: optional interface name to filter, e.g. 'Ethernet1'

tools.name: get_interfaces

tools.description: IPv4 routing table (FIB/RIB). Use for: 'how does it reach X', next-hop, default route, route to a prefix, VRF routing. Optionally filter by prefix and/or VRF.

device.description: target device (IP preferred; name/hostname OK); optional if only one device is configured

prefix.description: optional IPv4 prefix or address to look up, e.g. '10.0.0.0/24'

tools.name: get_ip_route

tools.description: Full running configuration as text. Use for: 'show me the config', auditing settings, finding how something is configured. For comparing two devices' configs use compare_config instead.

device.description: target device (IP preferred; name/hostname OK); optional if only one device is configured

tools.name: get_running_config

tools.description:
Fetch a curated read-only EOS dataset by topic. Most topic names say what they return (e.g. 'vlans', 'mac_address_table', 'arp_table'). For the IPv4 routing table with an optional prefix/VRF filter use get_ip_route; for anything with no topic use run_show_command. Hints for the less obvious topics:
version: EOS version, model, serial number, uptime
interface_counters: traffic and error counters: drops, discards, CRC
port_channels: LAG/EtherChannel summary and member state
bgp_summary: BGP IPv4 session states and prefix counts; start here for BGP
bgp_neighbors: per-neighbor BGP detail; use after bgp_summary
transceivers: optic/SFP DOM: Rx/Tx light levels
environment: power supplies, fans, temperatures
logging: 100 most recent syslog messages
processes: per-process CPU and memory snapshot
vxlan_interface: VNI-to-VLAN/VRF mappings and VTEP source interface
vxlan_vtep: remote VTEPs this switch has learned
vxlan_address_table: remote MAC to VTEP/VNI forwarding table
bgp_evpn_summary: EVPN control-plane session states; start here for EVPN
bgp_evpn: EVPN routes (Type-2/3/5); use after bgp_evpn_summary
ip_interface_brief: L3 interfaces with their IPv4 addresses
bfd_peers: BFD fast-failure-detection session state
route_summary: route counts by protocol (RIB scale)
ospf: OSPF process, areas, timers; pair with ospf_neighbors
pim_neighbors: PIM multicast routing adjacencies
igmp_snooping_groups: which ports joined which multicast groups
lacp_peers: LACP partner detail; pair with port_channels
ip_access_lists: IPv4 ACL rules with hit counters
inventory: chassis, line cards, PSUs, optics with serials
hardware_capacity: ASIC/TCAM table utilization against limits
qos_interfaces: per-port QoS trust mode, shaping, tx-queue mapping
storm_control: broadcast/multicast suppression thresholds per port
dhcp_relay: DHCP helper-address configuration
sflow: sFlow collectors, sample rate, datagrams sent
vrrp: first-hop redundancy: master/backup role, virtual IP
varp: anycast gateway virtual IP/MAC (EVPN/VXLAN fabrics)
ptp: PTP clock: grandmaster, offset-from-master, port roles
aaa: authentication/authorization/accounting method lists
tacacs: TACACS+ server reachability and counters
radius: RADIUS server reachability and counters
snmp_host: configured SNMP trap/notification receivers
macsec: link-encryption status per interface
macsec_counters: MACsec encrypted/protected counters and errors
tunnel_fib: GRE/VXLAN/MPLS tunnel forwarding entries
mpls_lfib: MPLS label forwarding: in/out labels, FEC
ldp_neighbors: LDP label-distribution session state
vxlan_counters: VXLAN tunnel-interface packet and byte counters

device.description: target device (IP preferred; name/hostname OK); optional if only one device is configured

tools.name: get_show_data

tools.description: List the device's gNMI capabilities (supported YANG models, encodings, versions). Use to discover what gNMI paths/models are available before gnmi_get/gnmi_subscribe.

device.description: target device (IP preferred; name/hostname OK); optional if only one device is configured

tools.name: gnmi_capabilities

tools.description: Fetch model-driven (OpenConfig) state/config via a gNMI Get for specific paths, returned as JSON. Use when the user asks for gNMI/OpenConfig data or a structured value at a known path. For CLI-style data prefer the get_* show tools.

device.description: target device (IP preferred; name/hostname OK); optional if only one device is configured

tools.name: gnmi_get

tools.description: Watch gNMI paths OVER TIME and collect telemetry updates for a bounded window, then return them. Use when the user wants to observe change/trend/live values (e.g. counters increasing, a flapping state). Modes: 'once' (single snapshot), 'sample' (periodic), 'on-change' (events). For a one-shot value use gnmi_get.

device.description: target device (IP preferred; name/hostname OK); optional if only one device is configured

max_updates.description: cap on number of updates to collect (default 500)

paths.description: gNMI paths to subscribe to, e.g. ['/interfaces/interface/state/counters']

sample_seconds.description: sample interval in seconds for 'sample' mode (default 10)

window_seconds.description: how long to collect updates, in seconds (default 15, max 60)

tools.name: gnmi_subscribe

tools.description: List the configured EOS devices and whether ad-hoc hosts are allowed. Call this FIRST when you don't know which devices exist or what to pass as 'device'.
tools.name: list_devices

tools.description: Ping a destination FROM a device to test reachability/latency. Use for 'can A reach B', connectivity checks, packet loss. Optional count/vrf/source.

destination.description: IP address or hostname to ping

device.description: target device (IP preferred; name/hostname OK); optional if only one device is configured

tools.name: ping_host

tools.description: Escape hatch: run an arbitrary read-only EOS command over eAPI. Use ONLY when no get_show_data topic or dedicated tool fits the request — prefer those (they return cleaner data). Write/config commands are rejected.

command.description: the read-only EOS command to run, e.g. 'show version'

device.description: target device (IP preferred; name/hostname OK); optional if only one device is configured

tools.name: run_show_command

tools.description: Traceroute from a device to a destination to see the hop-by-hop path. Use for 'what path does traffic take', locating where reachability breaks. Optional vrf.

destination.description: IP address or hostname to trace

device.description: target device (IP preferred; name/hostname OK); optional if only one device is configured

tools.name: traceroute_host

prompts.name: compare_devices

prompts.description: Run a full health review of a device and summarize findings.
prompts.name: device_health_review

prompts.description: Guide an investigation of BGP session problems on a device.
prompts.name: troubleshoot_bgp

prompts.description: Guide an investigation of a problematic interface on a device.
